items.title: Four Central Labour Codes commenced 21 November 2025
items.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
items.content: The four Labour Codes — Code on Wages, 2019 (Act 29 of 2019); Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (Act 35 of 2020); Code on Social Security, 2020 (Act 36 of 2020); Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (Act 37 of 2020) — have come into force with effect from 21 November 2025 across the country, as stated by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in PIB release PRID 2206144 dated 18 December 2025. Commencement is by Gazette notifications S.O. 5322(E) (Wages), S.O. 5319(E) (Social Security), S.O. 5320(E) (Industrial Relations) and S.O. 5321(E) (OSH&WC), all dated 21 November 2025. Do not treat pre-Code Acts (Payment of Wages Act 1936, Minimum Wages Act 1948, Industrial Disputes Act 1947, BOCW Act 1996, Unorganised Workers Social Security Act 2008, etc.) as currently operative where the corresponding Code provision has commenced. IMPORTANT EXCEPTION: under S.O. 5319(E), item 3 of section 164(1) of the Code on Social Security, 2020 (repeal of the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952) was NOT commenced.
items.notes: PIB is TIER 3 confirmatory. Gazette S.O. texts verified from copies hosted with labour.gov.in / prior session Gazette PDFs.
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND

F.No. S-32022/1/2025-WC. Alok Mishra, Jt. Secy.

items.title: Central Rules under the four Labour Codes notified 8 May 2026
items.content: On 8 May 2026 the Central Government notified implementing Central Rules (Gazette Part II, Section 3(i)): G.S.R. 342(E) Industrial Relations (Central) Rules, 2026; G.S.R. 343(E) Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026; G.S.R. 344(E) Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026; G.S.R. 345(E) Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026. They come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette (8 May 2026). They apply where the Central Government is the appropriate Government, unless the rule itself extends more widely. Wages (Central) Rules 2026 supersede Payment of Wages (Procedure) Rules 1937, Minimum Wages (Central) Rules 1950 and multiple other wage-related Central rules. Drafts were published 30 December 2025 (G.S.R. 930(E), 934(E), 935(E), 936(E)). These are RULES, not the parent Acts.

items.title: Statutory right to minimum wages for all employees (not only scheduled employments)
items.authority: Parliament of India / Ministry of Labour and Employment
items.section: Section 5 (as cited in MoLE explainer and Additional FAQs 16.03.2026)
items.eligibility: Employees employed in an establishment to whom the Code applies. MoLE Additional FAQs (16.03.2026) Q2: timely payment provisions are applicable to all employees. PIB PRID 2223852: 'A statutory right to all workers for minimum wages and timely payment of wages.'
items.benefit: Employer shall pay wages at not less than the minimum rates notified by the appropriate Government. Paying less than the prescribed minimum wage is legally prohibited (Additional FAQs Q3).
items.content: PIB PRID 2206144 (18 Dec 2025): Under the Code on Wages 2019 — universalisation of minimum wages to all employments as against scheduled employment in the previous Act. 'Floor Wage' has been made statutory which will be notified by the Central Government. Minimum rates of wages fixed by the appropriate Government shall not be less than floor wage. Additional FAQs on Labour Codes as on 16.03.2026, Q3: 'No, minimum wages are the statutory wages fixed by the appropriate government. An employer is legally prohibited from paying an employee less than the prescribed minimum wage.' Q9: Minimum wages are fixed by the Appropriate Government for the employees, whereas wages are fixed as per Terms of Employment. MoLE explainer: Employer shall pay minimum rates wages notified by appropriate government to employees (Section 5). LIMITATION: The numeric Central/State minimum wage for a given occupation/area is notified separately. This item does not itself contain a rupee amount. Floor wage amount as of 2026-09-11: NOT_FOUND in sources retrieved this session.
items.procedure: If paid less than notified minimum wage, worker may file a claim under section 45 of the Code on Wages, 2019 in Form-II under Rule 49 of the Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026 (where Central Government is appropriate Government), or corresponding State rules.
items.authority_responsible: Appropriate Government (Central or State). For Central sphere: Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) / Inspector-cum-Facilitator / authority under section 45.
items.limitations: Does not by itself create a rupee entitlement. Gig/platform workers are defined as outside traditional employer-employee relationship (SS Code); Code on Wages employee coverage of gig workers is NOT established by these sources.
items.notes: India Code full Act PDF could not be downloaded from this sandbox (bitstream 404). Section 5 citation is from MoLE explainer TIER 3, corroborated by Additional FAQs and PIB.

items.title: Definition of wages under Code on Wages section 2(y) and 50% add-back rule — effective 21.11.2025
items.content: Additional FAQs on Labour Codes (as on 16.03.2026) Q7: The definition of 'wages' has come into effect from 21.11.2025. Q6: Gratuity, based on revised definition of wages, will be applicable w.e.f. 21.11.2025. Q1 citing first proviso to section 2(y): Statutory components such as employer share of PF/Pension contribution are prescribed under Section 2(y)(c). If the total of items (a) to (i) of Section 2(y) exceeds 50% of remuneration/wages, the difference is added back to wages. Overtime allowance forms part of the 50 percent wage calculation. Gratuity, ESI and other retirement benefits are not included in that 50% computation (Q1). Annual performance-based incentives do not form part of wages (Q4). MoLE explainer Annexure (TIER 3): wages means all remuneration by way of salaries, allowances or otherwise, including (i) basic pay; (ii) dearness allowance; (iii) retaining allowance if any; excluding listed items including bonus under law, house-accommodation value, employer PF contribution, conveyance, HRA, overtime allowance, commission, gratuity, retrenchment compensation. If total of excluded items (a) to (i) exceeds 50% of total pay, excess is treated as wages. Remuneration in kind shall not exceed 15% of total wages. Q18 Additional FAQs: benefits under terms of employment such as food coupons, ration items, mobile recharge would constitute remuneration in kind.
items.limitations: Full statutory text of section 2(y) should be cited from India Code / Gazette Act when bitstream is available. FAQs carry a disclaimer that the Code prevails over FAQ text.
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Time limits for payment of wages (including 2 working days on exit)
items.section: Section 17 (exit payment — corroborated); wage-period section numbering CONFLICTING_SOURCES
items.content: MoLE explainer (labour.gov.in static PDF, 2026/02): Every establishment shall fix wage periods, which may be daily, weekly, fortnightly, or monthly. All wages must be paid within prescribed timelines: Daily — at the end of the day; Weekly — on the last working day of the week; Fortnightly — before the end of the second day after the end of the fortnight; Monthly — before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month. When an employee leaves an establishment, whether by resignation, dismissal, or termination, the employer is required to pay all due wages within two working days. (Explainer cites Section 17.) PIB PRID 2206144: 'Timely payment of wages to all employees.' Additional FAQs Q2: The Code on Wages, 2019 has provisions for timely payment of wages. These provisions are applicable to all employees. CONFLICT: The explainer attributes wage-period fixation to 'Section 6'. Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026 cite section 6 for fixation of minimum rate of wages (Rule 3 refers to section 6(5)), not wage periods. Treat wage-period TIMELINES as TIER 3 explainer content pending India Code section confirmation. Treat two-working-day exit payment as Section 17 per explainer. Do not invent a different deadline.
items.procedure: Worker whose wages are delayed may file a claim under section 45 / Rule 49 Form-II (Central sphere) or use SAMADHAN portal — see SAMADHAN conflict note.
items.limitations: Explainer section numbering for wage periods is not independently verified against India Code Act text in this session.
items.notes: CONFLICTING_SOURCES on which section number governs wage periods (explainer says s.6; Rules treat s.6 as minimum-wage fixation).
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Authorised deductions from wages shall not exceed 50 percent
items.content: Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026, Rule 13 Recovery of deductions: As per sub-section (4) of section 18, where the total deductions authorised under sub-section (2) of section 18 exceed fifty per cent. of the wages of an employee, the excess shall be carried forward and recovered from the wages of succeeding wage period, in instalments so that the recovery in any month shall not exceed the fifty per cent. of the wages of the employee in that month. MoLE explainer: Employers must not make any deductions except authorised under the Code. These include deductions for absence from duty, damage or loss, recovery of advances or loans, fines imposed after opportunity to be heard, house-accommodation or amenity on acceptance. Deductions shall not exceed 50% of wages during the wage period. (Section 18.) Rule 16: Procedure for imposing fines — employer shall give intimation specifying acts/omissions, show cause within seven days; if no reply, fine imposed and intimated within fifteen days. Rule 17: Deduction for absence — intimation, 7 days to reply. Rule 18: Deduction for damage or loss — opportunity to explain within 7 days showing cause of value of damage/loss of goods expressly entrusted. Rule 19: Recovery of advances in a wage period shall not exceed 50% of wages subject to Rule 13 ceiling. Authority for approving acts and omissions for fines (Rule 14): Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) having jurisdiction.
items.procedure: Challenge unauthorised or excess deductions via claim under section 45 / Form-II Rule 49.
items.authority_responsible: Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) for acts/omissions list; Inspector-cum-Facilitator; section 45 authority
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Overtime at not less than twice the normal rate of wages
items.document: Code on Wages, 2019 / OSH&WC Code, 2020 / Central Rules
items.section: Code on Wages section 14 (as cited in Rules/explainer); OSH&WC Additional FAQs Q24
items.eligibility: Additional FAQs Q5: Employee, including worker, whose minimum rate of wages is fixed under the Code on Wages, 2019 is eligible for overtime. MoLE explainer 3.2: If an employee whose minimum rate of wages has been fixed under the Code works beyond normal working hours, employer must pay overtime for each extra hour at a rate of at least twice the normal wage.
items.benefit: Not less than twice the normal rate of wages for overtime hours.
items.content: Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026 Rule 5: Normal working day for daily wage-period employee shall be eight hours; weekly hours for other wage periods shall not exceed forty-eight. Rest interval as per OSH&WC Code notification. Rule 6(4): work on rest day with substituted rest day — overtime rate not less than twice the normal rate of wages. Additional FAQs on Labour Codes 16.03.2026 Q24 (OSH&WC): The Code prescribes working hours as 8 hours per day. If a worker works for more than eight hours in any day as daily wager, or for more than forty-eight hours in any week, the worker shall in respect of such overtime work be entitled to wages at the rate of twice the normal rate of wages and shall be paid at the end of each wage period.
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Wage claim procedure — Form-II before authority under section 45 (Central Rules 2026)
items.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment / Chief Labour Commissioner (Central)
items.eligibility: Employees (or group of employees of same establishment for same wage period, or incident of discrimination). Application may be through employees concerned or registered trade union or Inspector-cum-Facilitator (Form-II heading).
items.procedure: 1. File a single application under section 45(5) in Form-II, manually or electronically, with documents specified in the Form, before the authority notified by Central Government under section 45(1). 2. Authority serves notice in Form VIII on employer electronically or by speed post to appear with documents and witnesses; informs applicant of date. 3. If employer fails to appear, authority may hear ex-parte. If applicant fails to appear without reasonable cause shown in advance, authority may dismiss. 4. Appeal: person aggrieved by order under section 45(2) may appeal under section 49(1) in Form-III electronically or by speed post. No employer appeal admitted unless claim amount deposited with appellate authority. 5. Offence enquiry: complaint before officer under section 53(1) by authorised officer, aggrieved employee, registered trade union, or Inspector-cum-Facilitator (Rule 53). APPLICABILITY: These Rules apply where Central Government is the appropriate Government. State sphere workers use corresponding State rules — not extracted here.
documents_required: Form-II particulars of employment and wage period
schedule of applicants if group claim
items.authority_responsible: Authority appointed under section 45(1) of Code on Wages, 2019 by Central Government; appellate authority under section 49; Inspector-cum-Facilitator under section 51
items.limitations: Does not itself specify the names/addresses of notified section 45 authorities. Worker-facing SAMADHAN portal still referenced old Acts as of last check — see conflict item.
items.notes: Form-II title: SINGLE APPLICATION UNDER SUB-SECTION (5) OF SECTION 45. CLC online-services page points workers to SAMADHAN for claims including minimum wage.

items.title: Prohibition of gender discrimination in wages and recruitment
items.section: Section 3 (as cited in MoLE explainer and PIB)
items.content: MoLE explainer: Employers must not discriminate on the basis of gender in paying wages for the same or similar work, and must not discriminate on the basis of sex while recruiting employees. (Section 3). PIB PRID 2206144: Promote gender neutrality and prohibit discrimination in recruitment and wage payment, including transgender.
items.procedure: Discrimination claims may be filed under section 45(5) as 'any incident of discrimination' per Rule 49(1).
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Legal definitions: aggregator, gig worker, platform worker, platform work
items.authority: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Labour and Employment
items.content: PIB document 'Labour Reforms: Formalising and Safeguarding India’s Gig & Platform Workforce' dated 9 December 2025 (static.pib.gov.in): The SS Code for the first time provides formal recognition to Gig workers and Platform workers, bringing them under the ambit of social security and legal protection. Definitions included: (1) Aggregator — a digital intermediary or a market place for a buyer or user of a service to connect with the seller or the service provider; (2) Gig worker — a person who performs work or participates in a work arrangement and earns from such activities outside of traditional employer-employee relationship; (3) Platform worker — a person engaged in or undertaking platform work; (4) Platform work — work arrangement outside of a traditional employer-employee relationship in which organisations or individuals use an online platform to access other organisations or individuals to solve specific problems or to provide specific services or any such other activities which may be notified by the Central Government, in exchange for payment. CRITICAL FOR DEACTIVATION/UNPAID PAY: These definitions place gig/platform work OUTSIDE the traditional employer-employee relationship. Sources do not state that Code on Wages employment-wage remedies automatically apply to gig/platform workers.
items.limitations: Does not create a right to reinstatement after platform deactivation. Does not convert gig workers into employees for wage-claim purposes.
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Aggregator contribution 1–2% of turnover (capped at 5% of amounts paid) — rate to be notified
items.content: PIB 9 Dec 2025 gig document: Under the SS Code, aggregators are now required to contribute 1-2% of their annual turnover (capped at 5% of payments made or payable to gig/platform workers) to a Social Security Fund. MoLE Additional FAQs 16.03.2026 Q15: 'As per section 114(4) of the Code on Social Security, 2020, the contribution to be paid by the aggregators for the funding Schemes for gig workers and platform workers will be notified by the Central Government. The said contribution will be credited to Social Security Fund set up by the Central Government for social security and welfare of the gig workers and platform workers.' Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 Rule 49(3)(a): Every aggregator shall assess contribution payable under section 114(4) in Form-XX and pay provisional contribution in the designated account of the Social Security Fund for the preceding year not later than 30th June of the current year. If paying on the basis of five per cent. of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers, this includes workers engaged directly or through associate/holding/subsidiary company or LLP or third party. Final return Form-XXI by 31 October. Interest on delayed contribution: one per cent. for every month or part of a month (Rule 49(2)). Contribution maintained in a separate account meant for gig and platform workers as specified in section 141(2) (Rule 49(1)(c)).
items.eligibility: Obligation is on aggregators, not on the worker. Worker benefits depend on schemes to be framed/notified.
items.benefit: Fund finances welfare schemes for gig and platform workers. Specific notified scheme benefits as of 2026-09-11: see limitations.
items.procedure: Aggregator files Form-XX (provisional by 30 June) and Form-XXI (final by 31 October). Worker does not file these forms.
items.authority_responsible: Central Government designated officer or agency to collect and expend aggregator contributions (Rule 49(1)(a))
items.limitations: The exact percentage between 1% and 2% is to be notified by the Central Government (FAQ Q15). WorkerSaathi must not treat a specific % as already notified unless a Gazette notification of the rate is produced. Specific gig social-security schemes funded from this contribution: CURRENT_STATUS_UNCONFIRMED as operational claim-ready schemes.

items.title: Registration of unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers — Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 Rule 48
items.subsection: (1) unorganised workers; (2) gig and platform workers
items.eligibility: Unorganised worker who has completed sixteen years of age (Rule 48(1)(a)). Gig and platform worker who has completed sixteen years of age (Rule 48(2)(a)). Registration on self-declaration basis with Aadhaar and other documents as prescribed, under section 113, on the designated Portal of the Central Government.
items.procedure: UNORGANISED: Apply electronically with Aadhaar via designated Central portal / mobile app. Appropriate Government to register their set of eligible unorganised workers. On completion, UAN or unique number issued if not already possessed. Digital identity card downloadable. Must update address, occupation, mobile, skill etc.; without updation may not be eligible for scheme benefits. CSC / Department of Posts business correspondents / e-sewa kendras may be used. GIG/PLATFORM: Self-register on designated portal. Additionally, every aggregator shall within 45 days of commencement of these rules share via API/electronic modes details of engaged gig/platform workers for UAN generation. New engagements: register in real time or daily via API. Exit details also to be shared real time or daily. Digital identity card issued.
documents_required: other documents as prescribed by Central Government by general or special order
items.benefit: Registration is a condition for benefits under schemes framed under the Code. Rule 48(1)(g): appropriate Government may notify additional eligibility conditions besides registration.
items.authority_responsible: Central Government (designated portal); appropriate Government for unorganised workers in their jurisdiction; aggregators for gig/platform worker data sharing
items.notes: Designated portal in practice is e-Shram (eshram.gov.in) as per PIB/MoLE annual report, though Rule 48 says 'designated Portal of the Central Government'.

items.title: Gig/platform scheme eligibility — 90 days (one aggregator) or 120 days (multiple) in last financial year
items.eligibility: To be eligible for any benefit under any scheme framed under the Code for gig and platform workers, Central Government may notify specific conditions, in addition to registration, PROVIDED that such eligible worker has been engaged as gig and platform worker for not less than ninety days with an aggregator, or in the case of multiple aggregators, not less than one hundred and twenty days, in the last financial year. Explanation: (i) engaged for one day if earned income, irrespective of amount, for work with the aggregator on that calendar day; (ii) multiple aggregators — days calculated cumulatively; (iii) engaged with three aggregators on a particular calendar day shall count as three days. Rule 49(4): A gig and platform worker registered under section 113 shall cease to be eligible for benefits of social security schemes when he attains the age of sixty years OR when he is not engaged as gig and platform worker with any of the aggregators for a period not less than ninety days, or in case of multiple aggregators not less than one hundred and twenty days, in the last financial year.
items.content: This is an eligibility condition for Code schemes, not a right to remain on a platform. Deactivation by an app is not addressed as an industrial dispute in these Rules.
items.limitations: Does not give a Central Government reinstatement remedy if a platform deactivates an account. Cessation of eligibility if days-of-engagement condition not met.
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Platform/gig account deactivation — no verified Central Government reinstatement right
items.authority: Research finding from Central sources reviewed 2026-09-11
items.content: Official Central sources reviewed (SS Code commencement, Social Security (Central) Rules 2026 Rules 48-49, PIB 9 Dec 2025 gig document, MoLE Additional FAQs, MoLE Annual Report extract, e-Shram pages) recognise gig/platform workers for social security and require aggregator contribution and registration. The PIB gig document states the appropriate Government MAY set up a toll-free helpline, call centre, or facilitation centre to address worker grievances. This is enabling language, not a notified operational deactivation-appeal procedure with forms and timelines. No Central Act/Rule/notification located in this research creates: (a) a right to be given reasons before deactivation; (b) a right to be reinstated on a platform; (c) a wage-claim as an 'employee' against an aggregator; (d) a SAMADHAN industrial-dispute pathway specifically for app deactivation. WorkerSaathi MUST answer: 'Insufficient verified Central Government information for a reinstatement/deactivation appeal. Worker may still: register/update on e-Shram; check scheme eligibility; seek NALSA legal aid if they qualify as industrial workman or other s.12 category (whether a gig worker is an industrial workman is UNVERIFIED); use platform's own grievance process (not a Central law). State labour departments / future notified helpline not imported here.'
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND as a Central statutory deactivation appeal. Related: e-Shram GMS (gms.eshram.gov.in) helpline 14434 is for e-Shram services, not platform deactivation.
items.limitations: Do not invent a Central complaint procedure for app deactivation.
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Social security benefits contemplated for gig/platform workers (scheme-dependent)
items.authority: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Labour and Employment
items.section: Section 114 (as described in PIB/Annual Report); Section 45 ESI schemes for unorganised/gig/platform (PIB PRID 2206144)
items.content: PIB 9 Dec 2025: Social security benefits include life & disability cover, health & maternity benefits, pension, accident insurance, and crèche. Gig & platform workers become eligible for government-notified social security benefits such as accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, any other benefits. Portability: unique Aadhaar-linked ID on e-Shram making benefits portable across platforms. PIB PRID 2206144: As per Section 45 of the Code on Social Security, 2020, the Central Government may, by notification, frame scheme for unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers and the members of their families for providing benefits admissible under Chapter IV (ESIC) by the Corporation. MoLE Annual Report extract (2026 upload): The Code provides for framing of suitable social security measures for gig workers and platform workers on matters relating to life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, old age protection, etc. 12 major platform aggregators onboarded on e-Shram: Zomato, Blinkit, Uncle Delivery, Urban Company, Uber, Amazon, Ola, Swiggy, Ecom Express, Rapido, Zepto and Porter. Advisories to aggregators 02.05.2025 and 23.07.2025.
items.benefit: Eligibility for GOVERNMENT-NOTIFIED schemes — not an automatic PF/ESI membership as an employee. Do not tell a delivery partner they are already entitled to a specific rupee insurance payout under s.114 unless a notified scheme so provides.
items.limitations: PIB language describes the framework. Operational claim-ready gig-only schemes funded by aggregator contribution: CURRENT_STATUS_UNCONFIRMED.
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Employer duty to notify workplace accidents and dangerous occurrences (OSH Central Rules 2026 Rule 7)
items.document: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026
items.section: Rule 7; parent Code sections 10, 11, 12 (as cited in MoLE explainer)
items.content: OSH&WC (Central) Rules, 2026, Rule 7 Notice of accidents and dangerous occurrences: (1) Accident resulting in death: employer shall inform Inspector-cum-Facilitator forthwith in FORM-XI and inform electronically and by telephone the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator(s), Inspector-cum-Facilitator(s), District Magistrate or Sub-divisional Officer and the officer-in-charge of the jurisdictional police station AND the family members or kin of the victim. (2) Accident resulting in bodily injury preventing work for 48 hours or more immediately following the accident: employer shall inform in FORM-XI within twelve hours after the completion of forty-eight hours, electronically to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator(s). (3) Dangerous occurrence (whether or not causing injury): employer shall within twelve hours send intimation to Inspector-cum-Facilitator and District Magistrate or Sub-divisional Officer. If death occurs later, forthwith telephone and electronic notice, confirmed in writing within twelve hours of death. MoLE explainer 5.7 cites parent Code: Section 10 (accident death/serious injury 48 hours/prescribed nature); Section 11 (dangerous occurrence); Section 12 (Third Schedule disease).
items.procedure: This is an EMPLOYER duty. A worker who is injured should still: seek medical care; note that family must be informed in death cases; may later claim ESI/disablement/dependants benefits if covered; may approach Inspector-cum-Facilitator / CLC; may seek NALSA legal aid. Worker complaint form to Inspector for accident: NOT_FOUND as a separate worker-initiated statutory form in the extracts (FORM-XI is employer notice).
items.authority_responsible: Inspector-cum-Facilitator; Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator; District Magistrate / Sub-divisional Officer; police in death cases
items.limitations: Rules apply where Central Government is appropriate Government unless otherwise provided. Construction sites in State sphere follow State OSH rules. ESI wage ceiling currently Rs 21,000/month until further notification (Additional FAQs Q12).
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Construction workplace safety duties (OSH Code as explained by MoLE)
items.document: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
items.content: MoLE explainer 5.13 Additional Provisions for Building or Other Construction Workers: Employer must provide free temporary living accommodation to all building workers at or near the worksite and ensure removal of such accommodation and restoration of land after use (Section 24). Principal Employer must pay expenses incurred by contractor for providing accommodation where work is through a contractor (Section 24). Employer must not employ any person who is known, or reasonably believed, to have hearing impairment, defective vision, or a tendency to giddiness in building or construction operations that may pose a risk of accident to themselves or others (Section 78). Employer must comply with occupational safety and health standards notified for BoCW by the Central Government (Section 18). PIB PRID 2223852 Provision 6: Safe and healthy working conditions for all workers. Provision 7: annual health check-up and issuance of appointment letters to all employees.
items.limitations: Section numbers from TIER 3 explainer, not independently extracted from India Code Act PDF this session.
items.notes: Building workers' welfare boards and most cash benefits remain State Board administered (see Rule 45). Do not import State board schemes.
items.eligibility: NOT_FOUND
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Registration of building workers — Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 Rule 45
items.eligibility: Building worker who has completed eighteen years of age and is less than sixty years of age and has been engaged in building or other construction work for not less than ninety days in the preceding twelve months (Rule 45(2) proviso).
items.procedure: Every employer or contractor shall register eligible building workers on their muster roll on the portal of the State Government or State Building Workers' Welfare Board or designated Central portal, within 30 days of becoming eligible, seeded with Aadhaar and UAN. State Board shall also register other eligible building workers in the State. Digital identity card issued. Portability: if worker moves to another State, employer/contractor of destination State shall obtain unique registration number and update destination State portal within 30 days; worker entitled to destination State Board benefits. Failure of employer to update shall not deny benefits. State Board shall provide grievance mechanism including telephone helpline, registration, renewal, updation, portability and delivery of welfare schemes (Rule 45(12)). Rule 46: If a building worker has been a beneficiary for at least three years continuously immediately before attaining age of sixty, Central Government may formulate schemes under which such worker shall be eligible.
items.benefit: Entitled to receive benefits provided by the State Building Workers' Welfare Board from its fund during validity of registration. Cash assistance through DBT. SPECIFIC benefit amounts: STATE-SPECIFIC — not extracted.
items.authority_responsible: State Building Workers' Welfare Board; employer/contractor; designated Central portal
items.limitations: Welfare benefits themselves are administered by State Boards. WorkerSaathi Central KB should say: register; then State Board schemes are a later phase. Rule 46 Central old-age schemes: 'may formulate' — not a currently quoted rupee pension.

items.title: ESI-type benefits for employment injury (SS Code Chapter IV) — coverage conditions
items.section: Section 32 (as cited in MoLE explainer); Additional FAQs Q12
items.eligibility: PIB PRID 2206144 / 2223852: ESIC coverage for establishments having more than 10 employees on mandatory basis; less than 10 on voluntary basis; even one employee if establishment involved in hazardous processes. ESIC coverage extended pan-India. Additional FAQs Q12: With effect from 21.11.2025 definition of wages under CoSS 2020 shall apply. At present, Rs 21,000 per month wages notified for ESI coverage will be applicable. Gig/unorganised: Central Government MAY notify ESIC Chapter IV schemes for them (s.45) — not the same as automatic ESI coverage.
items.benefit: MoLE explainer Section 32: Sickness benefit; Maternity benefit; Disablement benefit (periodical payments for disablement as a result of employment injury); Dependents' benefit (if employee died as a result of employment injury); Medical benefit for insured person and family; Funeral expenses.
items.content: Do not tell an informal construction or gig worker they automatically have ESI disablement benefit unless their establishment/coverage conditions are met or a notified s.45 scheme applies.
items.limitations: Rs 21,000 ceiling is 'at present until further notification'. Disablement rupee rates not extracted from Rules in this item.
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Grievance Redressal Committee — IR Code section 4 and IR (Central) Rules 2026 Rules 6–8
items.document: Industrial Relations (Central) Rules, 2026 / Industrial Relations Code, 2020
items.eligibility: Industrial establishment employing twenty or more workers. Aggrieved worker. MoLE explainer: application within one year from cause of action; GRC to complete proceedings within 30 days.
items.procedure: Rule 7: Aggrieved worker may file application stating grievance before Grievance Committee, with name, designation, worker code/token, department, length of service, category, address, contact, details of grievance and relief sought. May be sent electronically or otherwise. Shall be filed within one year from date cause of action arose. Rule 6: GRC equal employer and worker members, not exceeding ten; women representation not less than their proportion in workforce; term 3 years. Rule 8: Worker aggrieved by GRC decision OR whose grievance is not resolved within thirty days may file application online on designated portal of MoLE, or by speed post, or in person, within sixty days from GRC decision or from expiry of the period in section 4(6), to the conciliation officer through the Trade Union of which he is a member. Manual receipts to be digitised.
documents_required: application with identity and employment particulars
details of grievance and relief sought
items.authority_responsible: Grievance Redressal Committee of the establishment; conciliation officer; Regional Labour Commissioner (Central) for disputes on choosing worker representatives (Rule 6(5))
items.limitations: Applies to industrial establishments with 20+ workers in the Central sphere under these Rules. Gig platform deactivation is not shown as a GRC subject. Domestic households are not shown as industrial establishments in the extracted text.

items.title: SAMADHAN portal — worker industrial dispute and claims filing (content may still cite repealed Acts)
items.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment / Chief Labour Commissioner (Central)
items.eligibility: Workers with industrial disputes and other claims. CLC online-services page: online filling of industrial disputes and other claims of workers like Gratuity, Minimum wage, Equal Remuneration and Maternity benefits any allowance Dues etc.
items.procedure: CLC (https://clc.gov.in/clc/online-services) points to https://samadhan.labour.gov.in/ for online filling. Source registry notes homepage/FAQ historically listed Industrial Disputes Act 1947, Payment of Wages Act 1936, Minimum Wages Act 1948. PIB Year End Review 2025 said portal is under revamp for Codes. This session: samadhan.labour.gov.in returned HTTP 503 when fetched; FAQ PDF also failed to download.
items.limitations: CONFLICTING_SOURCES: portal historically maps claims to pre-Code Acts after 21 Nov 2025 commencement. Treat SAMADHAN as the official CLC-pointed online filing channel, but do not cite old Act section numbers from its FAQ as current law. Contact emails/phones from prior verified registry: samadhan-mole[at]gov[dot]in; 011-23473215 — re-verify when portal is up.
items.notes: Portal 503 on 2026-09-11 fetch. working status of live form UNVERIFIED this hour.

items.title: Shram Suvidha is an employer compliance portal, not a worker grievance forum
items.content: Shram Suvidha (https://shramsuvidha.gov.in/ and https://registration.shramsuvidha.gov.in/) is the Central employer-facing portal for LIN, registration, licence, inspection and returns, aligned with Labour Codes per ministry materials. WorkerSaathi must not send an unpaid-wage or injury complainant to Shram Suvidha as if it were a grievance portal. This session: shramsuvidha.gov.in browse failed to fetch; treat URL as official from MoLE/CLC ecosystem but page content not re-extracted this hour.
items.limitations: Not a worker complaint channel.

items.title: e-Shram registration eligibility, documents, process, helpline
items.eligibility: e-Shram Objectives page (last update 11-Sep-2026): Unorganised worker (UW); age 16 years or above at registration; not a member of EPFO/ESIC or NPS (Govt. funded). Definition quoted: Any worker who is a home based-worker, self-employed worker or a wage worker in the unorganised sector including a worker in the organised sector who is not a member of ESIC or EPFO or not a Govt. employee is called an Unorganised Worker. Categories listed: Construction Workers, Migrant Workers, Gig and Platform workers, Street Vendors, Domestic Workers, Agriculture Workers, etc. FAQ (beta.eshram.gov.in/faqs): age 16-59; no income criteria but should not be an income tax payee; no educational qualification other than gainful employment in unorganised sector. PIB PRID 2303053: Any worker aged 16 years and above engaged in unorganised sector; must not be income-tax payer or member of EPFO or ESIC. CONFLICT: Objectives page says 16 or above (no upper age); FAQ Q11 says 16-59. See conflicts file.
items.procedure: Self-register at https://eshram.gov.in / https://register.eshram.gov.in/#/user/self or via nearest CSC / State Seva Kendra. If no Aadhaar-linked mobile, visit CSC/SSK for biometric authentication. Free of charge. No last date. 24x7. UAN is 12-digit permanent number. e-Shram card never expires; no renewal, but keep details updated. Find CSC: https://findmycsc.nic.in/csc. Helpline: 14434 / 18008896811 (9.00 AM to 6.00 PM daily including Sundays). Grievance portal https://gms.eshram.gov.in. FAQ Q42: Right now, only registration is being done through e-Shram — no automatic cash benefit merely from registration.
documents_required: Aadhaar-linked mobile number (or biometric at CSC)
items.benefit: Facilitates delivery of social security benefits; UAN; digital identity; One-Stop-Solution mapping to other schemes. Registration itself is not a cash transfer (FAQ Q42).
items.limitations: e-Shram registration ≠ scheme enrolment. Each scheme has its own eligibility. GMS/helpline is for e-Shram services, not wage claims.

items.title: e-Shram One-Stop-Solution scheme mapping (statistics, not entitlements)
items.authority: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Labour and Employment
items.content: PIB PRID 2286757 dated 20 July 2026: e-Shram launched 26 August 2021. As on 14 July 2026, over 31.78 crore unorganised workers registered (Annexure-I total 31,78,31,749). eShram One-Stop-Solution launched 21 October 2024. Fifteen schemes integrated/mapped including PMSVANidhi, PMSBY, PMJJBY, VB-G RAM G, PMAY-G, AB-PMJAY, PMAY-U, PMMSY, PM-KISAN, ONORC, PMMVY; also NCS, SIDH, PM-SYM. Annexure-II enrolments of e-Shram registrants as on 14.07.2026 (STATISTICS ONLY — not a legal right arising from e-Shram card): AB-PMJAY 15,10,06,017; ONORC 24,46,15,089; PMSBY 8,53,50,770; PMJJBY 2,25,52,084; PMAY-G 98,40,347; PMAY-U 24,95,467; PM-KISAN 3,96,28,336; PMSVANidhi 32,66,698; PMMVY 32,04,450; VB-G RAM G 6,20,45,737; IGNWPS 11,75,748; IGNDPS 1,68,147; PMMSY 23,967.
items.limitations: DATASET/STATISTICS ≠ LEGAL AUTHORITY. Do not tell a caller they are entitled to PM-JAY merely because 15 crore e-Shram workers appear in a matching table.

items.title: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) pension scheme
items.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment / LIC as fund manager (as cited)
items.eligibility: PIB PRID 2293891: Workers aged 18 to 40 years whose monthly income is Rs. 15000/- or less and not a member of EPFO/ESIC/NPS (Contributed by Central Govt.) or not an income tax assessee. e-Shram schemes page: Indian Citizen; Unorganised Workers (street vendors, agriculture related work, construction site workers, leather, handloom, mid-day meal, rickshaw or auto, rag picking, carpenters, fishermen etc.); 18-40 years; monthly income below Rs.15000 and not a member of EPFO/ESIC/NPS (Govt. funded).
items.benefit: Monthly assured pension of Rs. 3000/- after attaining 60 years. On death of beneficiary, spouse eligible for 50% monthly pension. If husband and wife both join, they are eligible for Rs. 6000/- monthly pension jointly (e-Shram schemes page). PIB: pension disbursement will start not before February 2039 because scheme launched February 2019 (60-year vesting).
items.procedure: 50% monthly contribution by beneficiary and equal matching contribution by Central Government. Monthly contribution Rs. 55 to Rs. 200 depending on entry age. Self-enrol at https://maandhan.in / https://maandhan.in/maandhan/login ; also via CSC. As on 29.07.2026 more than 54 lakh enrolled (PIB 2293891).
documents_required: NOT_FOUND as a complete official list in pages fetched this session; Aadhaar typically required on e-Shram/PM-SYM ecosystem — do not invent a closed list
items.exclusions: EPFO/ESIC/NPS (Central Govt. contributed) members; income-tax assessees; age outside 18-40; monthly income above Rs 15000.
items.limitations: Gig/platform workers are not named as a distinct PM-SYM category on the e-Shram schemes extract; they may qualify only if they also meet unorganised-worker + income + age + exclusion tests. Do not auto-enrol a gig worker.

items.title: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
items.authority: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
items.eligibility: PIB PRID 2259251: All individual bank/Post office account holders of participating banks/Post office aged 18 to 50 years who give consent to join/enable auto-debit. One account only if multiple accounts. e-Shram page: Indian Citizen; 18 to 50; Jan Dhan or saving bank account with Aadhaar; auto-debit on consent.
items.benefit: Rs. 2 lakh payable on subscriber's death due to any cause. Lien period of 30 days from date of enrolment (PIB 2259251).
items.procedure: Premium Rs. 436/- per annum per member, auto-debit. Delayed enrolment pro-rata: June-Aug full Rs.436; Sep-Nov Rs.342; Dec-Feb Rs.228; Mar-May Rs.114. Enrol via bank/post office or Jan Suraksha Portal (jansuraksha.gov.in) / e-Shram One-Stop-Solution. Forms: https://www.jansuraksha.gov.in/Forms-PMJJBY.aspx
items.authority_responsible: Department of Financial Services; participating banks/post offices
items.limitations: Not a workplace injury ESI substitute. Claim process steps beyond portal mention: NOT_FOUND in PIB extract.

items.title: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — accident insurance
items.authority: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
items.eligibility: PIB PRID 2259251: Individual bank/Post office account holders of participating institutions aged 18 to 70 years with consent for auto-debit. One enrolment across multiple accounts.
items.benefit: PIB table: (a) Death Rs. 2 Lakh; (b) Total and irrecoverable loss of both eyes or loss of use of both hands or feet or loss of sight of one eye and loss of use of hand or foot Rs. 2 Lakh; (c) Total and irrecoverable loss of sight of one eye or loss of use of one hand or foot Rs. 1 Lakh. e-Shram page paraphrase: Rs. 2 lakh accidental death and full disability; Rs. 1 lakh partial disability. Premium Rs. 20/- per year.
items.procedure: Premium Rs.20/- per annum auto-debit. Enrol via bank/post office or jansuraksha.gov.in / e-Shram. Forms: https://jansuraksha.gov.in/Forms-PMSBY.aspx
items.authority_responsible: Department of Financial Services; participating banks/post offices
items.notes: Useful for workplace accident conversation BUT it is a bank-account accident insurance scheme, not a substitute for ESI disablement benefit or employer accident liability under OSH/SS Codes.

items.title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
items.authority: Department of Financial Services / PFRDA (as commonly administered; PIB DFS release)
items.eligibility: PIB PRID 2259251: Open to all bank account holders aged 18 to 40 years who are not income tax payers. e-Shram: Indian citizen; 18-40; bank account linked with Aadhaar.
items.benefit: Guaranteed minimum monthly pension of Rs. 1000 or 2000 or 3000 or 4000 or 5000 after age 60 based on contributions. After subscriber, spouse; after both, corpus at 60 returned to nominee. If subscriber dies before 60, spouse may continue contribution till original 60.
items.procedure: Contributions differ based on pension amount chosen. Forms cited on e-Shram page: https://www.npscra.nsdl.co.in/nsdl-forms.php. Also Jan Suraksha portal ecosystem.

items.title: Ayushman Bharat — PM-JAY health cover (SECC occupational criteria include domestic and construction workers)
items.authority: National Health Authority / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
items.eligibility: NHA page nha.gov.in/PM-JAY (web search extract): inclusion based on SECC 2011 deprivation and occupational criteria. About 12 crore households. Rural: D1-D5 and D7 plus automatic inclusion (destitute/living on alms, manual scavenger, primitive tribal group, legally released bonded labour). Urban occupational categories include: ragpicker; beggar; domestic worker; street vendor/cobbler/hawker; construction worker/plumber/mason/labour/painter/welder/security guard/coolie; sweeper/sanitation worker/mali; home-based worker/artisan/handicraft/tailor; transport worker/driver/conductor/helper/cart puller/rickshaw puller; shop worker/assistant/peon/helper/delivery assistant/attendant/waiter. PIB Aug 2025 (doc2025830624501): Union Budget 2025-26 announced healthcare coverage under AB-PMJAY for online platform workers; 'The AB-PMJAY scheme for platform workers is yet to be launched' as of that August 2025 document. Status of launch as of 2026-09-11: CURRENT_STATUS_UNCONFIRMED from NHA page (page 503 this session).
items.benefit: AB-PMJAY provides a cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation across over 31,000 public and private empanelled hospitals in India (PIB Aug 2025 document).
items.limitations: e-Shram matching statistics do not create PM-JAY eligibility. Platform-worker-specific PM-JAY module launch: UNCONFIRMED as of this verification date. nha.gov.in returned 503 this session; eligibility extracted from search-indexed NHA content and PIB.
items.procedure: NOT_FOUND

items.title: Free legal aid eligibility — Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 section 12
items.eligibility: NALSA https://nalsa.gov.in/legal-aid/ quoting Section 12: entitled if: (1) SC or ST; (2) victim of trafficking or begar (Art. 23); (3) a woman or a child; (4) mentally ill or otherwise disabled person; (5) person under circumstances of undeserved want (mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster); (6) an industrial workman; (7) person in custody (protective home / juvenile home / psychiatric hospital as specified); (8) person with annual income less than the scheduled State ceiling (or higher amount prescribed by State Government) if case is before a court other than Supreme Court, and less than Rs 5 Lakh if case is before the Supreme Court (legal-aid page). FAQ: woman entitled irrespective of income (s.12(c)). Child till 18. Industrial workman eligible (FAQ explicit yes). CONFLICT: FAQ first Q&A says Supreme Court income less than rupees twelve thousand or higher amount prescribed by Central Government — this appears stale versus legal-aid page Rs 5 lakh and FAQ later paragraph Rs 5 lakh. Flag CONFLICTING_SOURCES on SC income ceiling. Whether a gig worker or domestic worker is an 'industrial workman' under this Act: NOT_FOUND in NALSA pages. Do not assume. Women workers qualify regardless.
items.procedure: Approach Taluk Legal Services Committee, District Legal Services Authority, State Legal Services Authority, High Court Legal Services Committee or Supreme Court Legal Services Committee. Offline form, post, online (nalsa.gov.in), email nalsa-dla@nic.in, or oral with paralegal volunteer. No fee. Helpline 15100 (promoting-inclusive-legal-system page). Phones 011-23382778, 23071450, 011-23382121. Address: B Block, Ground Floor, Additional Building Complex, Supreme Court of India, New Delhi-110001. Communication: Jaisalmer House, 26 Man Singh Road, New Delhi-110011. Decision within 7 days per Regulation 7(2) as stated on legal-aid page. Assigned panel lawyer. Expenses borne by institution.
documents_required: SC/ST certificate if claiming that category
income affidavit (s.13(2) generally sufficient unless questioned)
items.benefit: Representation by advocate, drafting, court fees/expenses, advice, access to welfare benefits, all courts/tribunals including Supreme Court.
items.authority_responsible: NALSA / State / District / Taluk Legal Services Authorities
items.limitations: WorkerSaathi is not a lawyer and must not give case-specific legal advice. Point eligible workers to NALSA. Income ceilings vary by State for the residual income category — those ceilings are State-prescribed (table on FAQ) and should be used only as NALSA-published information, not as State labour law.

items.title: Domestic workers — Central coverage is registration/schemes; employment-law applicability UNVERIFIED
items.content: e-Shram lists Domestic Workers among unorganised workers who may register. PM-JAY urban SECC occupational list includes 'Domestic worker'. PM-SYM e-Shram description includes domestic workers among example unorganised occupations (PIB Hindi extract PRID 2108189). No Central Code extract in this research states that a private household is an 'establishment' for Code on Wages claims, OSH accident notice, or IR GRC. Do not tell a domestic worker that SAMADHAN/Form-II definitely applies. Do tell them: e-Shram registration; check PM-SYM/PMJJBY/PMSBY/PM-JAY eligibility; NALSA (women eligible irrespective of income); State domestic-worker laws are out of scope for this Central KB.
